hook.line: Hernando's memoir is full of people who changed in the end: a father who gave in, a friend who went too far. Two small phrases tell those stories, and they are easy to swap.

examples.en: He even came to hate it.

examples.es: Hernando acabó por contarle todo a Tomás.
examples.en: Hernando ended up telling Tomás everything.

examples.es: Llegó a vender el carro para pagar la deuda.
examples.en: He even sold the car to pay off the debt.

examples.es: Después de tres años, Rosa acabó por perdonarlo.
examples.en: After three years, Rosa ended up forgiving him.
He never got as far as telling me.

examples.es: Llegué a pensar que no volvías.
examples.en: I even started to think you weren't coming back. (to a friend)

rule:
Both phrases say where things ended up, but they look at different things.

*Acabar por* + infinitive is the end of a process, often after doubt or resistance. It is what was left in the end: *Acabó por aceptarlo*. 'He ended up accepting it.' Everyday cousins: *acabó aceptándolo*, *terminó aceptándolo*.

*Llegar a* + infinitive is how far things went, often a surprising extreme: *Llegó a odiarlo*. 'He even came to hate it.' With *no*, it means he never got that far: *No llegó a decírmelo*.

Two tests. Did it finally end that way? *Acabar por*. Did it go as far as that? *Llegar a*. And remember the little words: *acabar por*, *llegar a*.
smallPrint: Teachers call both of these aspectual periphrases of an end point: *acabar por* marks the outcome, *llegar a* marks the limit reached.

options: He ended up accepting it.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *acabó por* or *llegó a*: after holding out, Hernando finally signed. Hernando ___ firmar el papel. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Hernando acabó por firmar el papel.
yourTurn.why: He finally gave in at the end, so *acabó por*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *acabó por* or *llegó a*: he went as far as selling his car. Hernando ___ vender el carro. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Hernando llegó a vender el carro.
yourTurn.why: Selling the car is an extreme he reached, so *llegó a*.

yourTurn.prompt: He never got as far as telling me.
yourTurn.why: *No llegó a* says he never reached that point.

yourTurn.prompt: After three years, Rosa ended up forgiving him.
yourTurn.answer: Después de tres años, Rosa acabó por perdonarlo.
accept: Rosa acabó por perdonarlo después de tres años.
Después de tres años, Rosa acabó perdonándolo.
yourTurn.why: Three years of resistance, then the outcome: *acabó por*.

yourTurn.prompt: I even started to think you weren't coming back. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Llegué a pensar que no volvías.
accept: Llegué a pensar que no ibas a volver.
yourTurn.why: It marks how far your worry went, so *llegué a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about we: *Acabó por aceptarlo.*
Make it about I: *Llegó a quererlo.*
yourTurn.why: *Llegué* is the *I* form, and *a quererlo* stays the same.

pitfalls.wrong: Llegó a aceptarlo, después de dudar mucho.
pitfalls.right: Acabó por aceptarlo, después de dudar mucho.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A long struggle that ends with giving in is the job of *acabar por*.
*Acabar* takes *por* before the infinitive; *llegar* is the one with *a*.
To say he never got that far, put *no* before *llegó*.

personal: Finish one sentence about yourself: *Con los años, llegué a…* for something that went further than you expected, or *Al final, acabé por…* for something you gave in to.
